about.title: La Cañada Flintridge Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, often in places locals visit routinely — a grocery store off Foothill Boulevard, a shopping strip near the I-210 interchange, or a trailhead parking area along Angeles Crest Highway. What's harder is proving the property owner should have caught the hazard before you did. California law puts the burden on showing the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the dangerous condition and didn't fix it or warn visitors. That's why documenting the scene matters so much: photos of the spill, torn carpet, or uneven pavement, along with witness names and any surveillance footage before it's erased, can shape the entire claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself — we simply connect injured people in La Cañada Flintridge with an independent attorney who handles these evaluations at no upfront cost, working on contingency so there's no fee unless you recover something.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Fall Here

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can help gather the evidence — inspection logs, prior complaints, maintenance records — that speaks to that notice requirement.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of footage from a store or property near Foothill Boulevard can make a real difference in what's available later.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Recovery
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, even if you're found partly responsible for a fall, you may still recover a share of damages reduced by your percentage of fault rather than being barred entirely.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in La Cañada Flintridge?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity — say, a public building or city-maintained space — that window shrinks dramatically and requires an earlier claim, so it's worth getting this checked promptly.

items.question: I fell at a store near the I-210 corridor but wasn't sure what caused it. Does that matter?
items.answer: It matters quite a bit — pinpointing the specific hazard, whether it was a wet floor, a loose mat, or poor lighting, helps establish what the property owner should have noticed and fixed. Taking photos right after the fall, even from your phone, can help an attorney reconstruct that picture later.

items.question: What if I was partly distracted or not looking down when I fell?
items.answer: California's comparative fault rules mean you can still pursue a claim even if you share some blame, though any compensation would be reduced by your percentage of fault. An independent attorney can review the specifics of your fall to explain how that might apply to your situation.
